description: This course provides a comprehensive practical understanding of automation technologies covering sensors, actuators, drive systems and control techniques. Students learn to implement real-time data acquisition, feedback control and precision automation using microcontrollers and programmable logic controllers. The course emphasizes hands-on experimentation with proximity and distance sensors, stepper and servo drives, motor control algorithms and real-time automation challenges.
experiments: Perform performance analysis of proximity and distance sensors for object detection and range measurement.
Control motors using various drive systems, including servo, stepper and DC drives.
Implement real-time data acquisition and feedback control using microcontrollers such as Arduino or Raspberry Pi.
Develop a basic program and control logic to turn an LED on and off at regular intervals using Arduino or Raspberry Pi.
Achieve real-time bed levelling using stepper motors and proximity sensors in a 3D printer.
Study the relationship between extrusion motor speed, temperature and layer consistency in fused deposition modeling.
Study single-acting and double-acting piston-cylinder mechanisms for a pneumatic system.
Study the working principle of an LVDT and characterize it by determining its linear range, sensitivity, non-linearity and hysteresis.
Perform object detection and generate a 3D map of a scene using depth data from a Time of Flight sensor.
Implement a gesture-recognition system using a Time of Flight sensor to control a robotic arm.
outcomes: Analyze and compare the performance of various proximity and distance sensors for object detection and range measurement.
Implement and control different drive systems, including servo, stepper and DC motors.
Develop real-time data acquisition and feedback control using microcontrollers such as Arduino and Raspberry Pi.
Investigate the effect of extrusion speed, temperature and layer consistency in FDM-based additive manufacturing.
Understand and analyze pneumatic actuation systems, including single-acting and double-acting piston-cylinder mechanisms.
Characterize the working principles of an LVDT sensor by determining parameters such as sensitivity, linearity and hysteresis.
